sections.html:
Reno is the seat of Washoe County, tucked against the California line in the Truckee River valley below the Sierra Nevada. Elevation is around 4,400 feet, and Lake Tahoe lies about 23 miles to the southwest. The 2020 census counted 264,165 residents. The University of Nevada, Reno and the casino and tourism trade shape much of the housing market, and Reno shares the Truckee Meadows valley with Sparks.

Houses here run from older central neighborhoods to hillside and western-edge homes, so condition, exposure and lot all affect what a buyer will offer.

sections.h2: Winter, wind and what they do to a house
sections.html:
Reno has cold, dry winters and hot summers, so a single year can bring a deep freeze, high wind and long stretches of heat. Temperatures hit freezing or lower on 122 days a year, while about 65 days reach 90 degrees or more. The record low is minus 17 degrees and the record high 108. Most moisture falls in fall, winter and spring, and the western side of town gets three to four times what the east side does.

Wear shows up in predictable places:

  • Pipes, hose bibs and exterior paint, after repeated freeze and thaw
  • Roofing and fencing, battered by wind and big temperature swings
  • Western-edge properties, which see far more precipitation than eastern ones

Deferred maintenance on any of this is not something you must fix before a cash sale. Defects you know about belong on the Nevada disclosure form.

sections.h2: How much wildfire and earthquake risk does Reno have?
sections.html:
Wildfire is the largest natural hazard for Reno homes, especially on the southwest side, and most homes in the area carry some risk. A few events show how real that is:

EventWhat happened
November 2011 Caughlin firePowerline arcing started a fire in southwest Reno that destroyed 26 homes
January 2012 Washoe Drive fireFireplace ashes started a fire that destroyed 29 homes, with about 10,000 people evacuated
September 2024 Davis FireForested areas of southwest Reno burned, 14 structures were lost and about 20,000 people were evacuated
February 2008 earthquake swarmThe largest quake was about magnitude 4.9, centered near Somersett, Mogul and Verdi, and many homes were damaged

If your house backs onto a forested edge, say so on the disclosure form, along with any smoke or fire damage.

Reno's Code Enforcement department handles property maintenance, and an open violation can end up recorded against your title. The municipal code covers inoperable vehicles, trash and debris, overgrown landscaping, work without permits and zoning violations. The usual sequence runs like this:

  1. A warning of violation letter sets a compliance date, generally about 30 days out.
  2. If the problem remains, an administrative citation follows: $100 the first time, $250 the second and $500 the third on residential property.
  3. A notice of intent to record can lead to a notice of violation lien filed with the Washoe County Recorder.
  4. The lien comes off only after the work is fixed and all fines and fees are paid.

Owners can appeal through the City Clerk's office, and code officers have no authority to waive or reduce fines. Questions and complaints go to Reno Direct at 775-334-4636.

Some common problems sellers overlook: vehicles cannot be parked in the front yard, inoperable ones must be screened, and couches, mattresses and appliances cannot sit in view in a front or side yard. Tidy these up before photos or a walkthrough, and find out whether a lien has already been recorded. The city's 2024 building codes took effect July 1, 2025, so if you are finishing unpermitted work before a sale, check permit status with Building first.

sections.h2: What does Nevada require from a Reno seller?
sections.html:
A Reno seller completes the state disclosure form at least 10 days before conveyance, and cash deals are not exempt. Under NRS 113.130 the owner, not the agent, fills it out, and the buyer cannot waive it. The exceptions cover foreclosure sales, transfers between spouses or close relatives and some trustee or personal representative sales.

If the home belongs to a homeowners association, the resale package in NRS 116.4109 must go to the buyer, who has five calendar days after receiving it to cancel.

Washoe County tacks $0.10 onto the statewide transfer tax, which makes the rate $2.05 per $500 of value. The Recorder collects it when the deed is recorded. A Declaration of Value form has to accompany any document that transfers title. The value used is the sale price or the estimated fair market value, taken from the assessor's taxable value or a purchase price within the last five years, whichever is higher.

State guidance makes buyer and seller both liable, so the contract should say who pays. The Property Transfer Compliance Recorder answers questions at (775) 328-3661.

sections.h2: Washoe County property tax for sellers
sections.html:
The Washoe County Treasurer bills property tax, mailing bills by August 1 each year. For 2026-27 the installments still ahead fall on January 4 and March 1, and a parcel with more than $100 of tax can pay in four. Delinquent property is advertised, and owners have two years from the lien filing to redeem it.

The Assessor handles values and the tax cap. Under Assembly Bill 489, passed in 2005, the cap limits growth in the tax bill, not the assessed value, at 3 percent on a primary residence, with a higher cap on other property. After a change of ownership the Assessor mails an affidavit, and the property stays at the higher cap until a qualifying one is filed. Raise that with a buyer. Appeals of value go to the County Board of Equalization by January 15.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Reno
sections.html:
A cash buyer skips lender underwriting, so title work and the recording step at the Washoe County Recorder set the pace. An address and a rough description of the condition are enough to request an offer. We charge no fees or commissions, and you owe nothing if you pass.

Expect to hand over the disclosure form, clear any recorded code liens and confirm your tax status. We buy Reno houses as-is, including ones with deferred maintenance, tenants or probate issues.

A typical Reno closing goes in this order: you accept a written offer, a title company opens escrow and searches the Washoe County records, you sign the disclosure form and any HOA package, and the deed is recorded with a Declaration of Value. Taxes owed and any recorded lien are paid from your proceeds. Because no appraisal or loan committee is involved, the date is usually set by when you want to move, not by a lender.

faqs.q: Is Reno at risk of wildfire?
faqs.a: Yes, mainly on the southwest side. Most homes in the area carry some risk, and the September 2024 Davis Fire burned 14 structures and led to about 20,000 evacuations.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Reno home sale?
faqs.a: Washoe County's rate is $2.05 per $500 of value, the $1.95 statewide rate plus $0.10. The County Recorder collects it at recording, and buyer and seller are both liable.

faqs.q: Can Reno code enforcement put a lien on my house?
faqs.a: Yes. After warnings and citations the city can record a notice of violation lien with the Washoe County Recorder. It is released once the violation is fixed and all fines and fees are paid.

faqs.q: Do I have to make repairs before a cash sale in Reno?
faqs.a: No repair is required by the sale itself. You must still list known defects on the seller's disclosure form at least 10 days before conveyance, and open code violations or unpermitted work are worth raising with the buyer.

faqs.q: When is the Washoe County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Appeals to the County Board of Equalization are due by January 15, or the next business day if that falls on a weekend or holiday. A decision can be appealed to the State Board of Equalization by March 10.
